hook.line: In Spanish the verb you choose to report someone does half the talking. "He said" is neutral, but *soltó*, *aclaró* and *insinuó* tell your listener how you took it, and you can be held to that.
hook.es: Me soltó que ya se encargaría otro.
hook.en: He blurted out that someone else would take care of it.

examples.es: Me soltó que ya se encargaría otro.
examples.en: He blurted out that someone else would take care of it.

examples.es: Me reprochó que no hubiera ido.
examples.en: She reproached me for not having gone.

She hinted that I had lied.

examples.es: Hernando me soltó que el café se vendería.
examples.en: Hernando blurted out to me that the café would be sold.

examples.es: El senador insinuó que Altamira había pagado.
examples.en: The senator hinted that Altamira had paid.

rule:
Pick the verb that matches how it sounded:
*soltar que* (it just slipped out)
*aclarar que* (made it clear)
*insinuar que* (hinted)
*reprochar que* (blamed me for it)

After *soltar*, *aclarar* and *insinuar* the news stays in the normal tenses, shifted back when the report is in the past (*había mentido*, *estaba*).
After *reprochar* the news takes the subjunctive: *que no hubiera ido*.

To report an order, use *que* too: *Me dijo que lo llamara*, never an infinitive.
smallPrint: Teachers call these verbs of speech that interpret: the verb adds your reading of what was said.

options: She stated plainly that I had lied.
She hinted that I had lied.
She regretted that I had lied.

options: She reproached me for not having gone.

She hoped that I would not go.

options: He blurted out that he was against it.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Me ___ que ya se encargaría otro.* (*soltó* or *reprochó*) He blurted out that someone else would take care of it.
yourTurn.answer: Me soltó que ya se encargaría otro.
yourTurn.why: It just slipped out, so *soltó*, and the news stays in the normal tenses.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Insinuó que yo ___ mentido.* (*había* or *he*) She hinted that I had lied.
yourTurn.why: The report is in the past, so "have lied" shifts back to *había mentido*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: She reproached me for not having gone.
yourTurn.answer: Me reprochó que no hubiera ido.
yourTurn.why: After *reprochar* the news takes the subjunctive, here *hubiera ido*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: He made it clear that he wasn't against it.
yourTurn.answer: Aclaró que no estaba en contra.
yourTurn.why: *Aclarar que* is followed by plain tenses, shifted back.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The senator hinted that Altamira had paid.
yourTurn.answer: El senador insinuó que Altamira había pagado.
yourTurn.why: *Insinuó que* plus *había pagado* for something already done.

yourTurn.prompt: Change the verb to *hinted*: *Me soltó que Vale había mentido.*
yourTurn.answer: Me insinuó que Vale había mentido.
yourTurn.why: Only the verb changes, since the news keeps its normal tenses.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Tomás reproached Vale for not calling.
yourTurn.answer: Tomás le reprochó a Vale que no llamara.
accept: Tomás le reprochó que Vale no llamara.
yourTurn.why: *Reprochar* is followed by the subjunctive, so *llamara*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "told me to call him", but Spanish reports an order with *que* and the subjunctive, never an infinitive.

pitfalls.right: Me reprochó que no hubiera ido.
